best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers a 10% unconditional Healing% boost and an most importantly a 15% ATK% boost for the entire team, lasting 30 seconds whenever you heal yourself or any of your allies. This bonus can be triggered by character abilities and weapon effects, is easy to keep active 100% of the time and is a big help for all party members.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Simple summon Echo that can be cast any time (ideally right before the wielder's Outro), granting 10% ATK to the team for 20s (sufficient for 2 other teammates' rotation times if cast right before Outro) as well as 10% Energy Regen to the wielder to help with Energy requirements.

best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers a 10% unconditional Energy Regen% boost taking some pressure off your gear when aiming at ER breakpoints. Also upon using Outro, grants the next character switching in a 22.5% ATK boost, amplifying any of your main damage dealers burst windows.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Supportive Echo that can be run at the cost of a sizeable chunk of damage for the character who equips, trading personal gain for team benefits. Should always be used and immediately switch cancelled right before performing an Outro, leading to another DPS. When done so will grant the next character switching in 12% increased DMG% which when combined with the 5P Moonlit set which also grants 22.5% ATK% under the same conditions makes for a sizeable boost. While the echo does lower the damage of whoever wears it, it grants a massive chunk of energy on use usually saving 1 or sometimes even 2 Energy Regen sub stats that may otherwise be needed by the wearer allowing for some damage to be recovered.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Shorekeeperâs signature weapon is not only amazing for her but also for any Rectifier support. Granting insane amounts of Energy Regen as its secondary stat, increasing the equipped characterâs HP all the while providing additional Concerto Energy when casting your Ultimate is seriously valuable for any support that can equip the weapon. It additionally provides a team-wide ATK buff if the equipped characterâs Resonance Skill is used and it provides healing, which makes it stand out as an amazing support weapon.

When casting Resonance Skill that heals, increase nearby party members' ATK by {2} for 30s. Effects of the same name cannot be stacked.

best_weapons.commentary_details: A utility-focused weapon prioritizing lightning-fast Concerto rotations over raw output with the ability to transform entire units' action priorities under the right circumstances. Not always a good choice but when implemented correctly makes all the difference. Also offers an immense amount of Energy Regen further accelerating rotations and supportive capabilities.

weapon_base_info.effect_description: When Resonance Skill is released, restores Concerto Energy by {0}. This effect can be triggered 1 time every 20s.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Best weapon choice if you don't have Concerto weapons available, acquired for free via Rinascita Exploration Quests, which gives a great amount of Energy Regen and an extra Healing Bonus boost upon casting Ultimate for higher sustain.

weapon_base_info.effect_description: Casting Resonance Liberation increases the Resonator's Healing Bonus by {0} for 15s.

best_weapons.commentary_details: An easily accessible supportive option with a reasonable amount of Energy Regen. It also grants the unique ability to gain a sizable chunk of raw Resonance Energy once every 20 seconds. For most character's rotations in teams, this bonus will be ready every time it's their turn to switch-in, making this weapon a great choice for any character who doesn't need damage but needs their Ultimate fast and has trouble accessing it otherwise. The flat energy gain is more powerful the less energy the character and team they are a part of can generate. This weapon is preferred over certain 4-star Rectifier options that give Energy Regen such as Rectifier#25 as the flat Energy boost from this weapon's passive is more effective at granting Resonance Energy.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Decent F2P craftable option that provides a lot of Energy Regen, some additional HP restore and some ATK% depending on your current HP situation. Little value beyond the Energy Regen and small ATK% boost.

cons: 15% ATK buff only applies to one character and requires to be picked up from the ground in a random spot - so impractical it's usually just better to skip out on it unless it's picked up by pure chance, with few exceptions;
Outro only applies to the active character, so off-field attackers don't benefit and Quickswap buffing is very restricted;

SUPER inconsistent. Quite literally unusable against highly mobile/airborne enemies because her hits need to connect to generate Forte, which is needed to finish her rotation. Rotations can take ages as a result;
Dodge Counters and swap-in attacks don't generate any Forte, so aggressive enemies slow down her rotation even more based on enemy type and Quickswap use is even harder;

Completely outclassed by both Verina (in all cases) and Buling (in 95% of cases), even if she's S6 and the other two are S0. Very unlikely you'll actually have a legitimate use case for her unless you really want some extra low-scoring Matrix teams.
pros: Requires basically no resources to build (at least very few);

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Baizhi is a 4-star Glacio Rectifier generalist Support character who was one of the very first generalist buffing healers to be released in the game. She relies on long-range combat with her Remnant Creature You'Tan, which she throws at enemies to attack with.

sections.heading: Key Mechanics & Rotation Concepts
paragraphs: Baizhi's an extremely simple character in concept. Her rotation goal is to cast her Outro as quickly as possible. She has two ways of consuming Forte, and one way of generating it. She can gain up to 4 Forte points, each earned by doing one Basic Attack. When her Forte has any amount of stacks added, she can consume it via either her Skill or her Heavy Attack to generate bursts of Concerto Energy. Her Skill gives 8 Concerto per stack consumed, but is on a pretty big 16s cooldown, while her Heavy Attack gives 4 per stack, but has no cooldown.

Her rotation varies significantly based on the weapon she has equipped. The lower rank your Concerto weapon, the more field time she'll have to use up to get her rotations done. Generally, Baizhi will want to cast her Skill with full Forte stacks, to consume them all at once, since the Concerto Energy generation is that much more efficient but the cooldown gates it to one use per rotation.

Otherwise, it practically always boils down to this: Use Basic Attacks until you have 4 stacks, use Skill to consume them, use your Ultimate somewhere to get the extra Concerto boost from it, finish what's left with some extra Basics and a Heavy Attack. Baizhi has a pretty bad Intro and swap-in attack that she's forced to rely on occasionally, and her Dodge Counter also doesn't help since all of them don't give her any Forte stacks.

Baizhi has some healing upon consuming Forte stacks, her Intro and Outro, as well as her Skill and Ultimate. In fact, her Ultimate also spawns a few Coordinated Attacks at a rate of one hit every 2.5s (4 to 6 times based on her Sequences) that generate some healing on hit.

Finally, her Outro restores HP continuously to the active character every 3s, and grants them 15% DMG Amplification for 6s when the healing is triggered. One of her passives also allows her to generate a feather called Euphonia on the ground. It gives a 15% ATK buff to the character who picks it up for 20s. However, due to its random placement often requiring extra movement that can cost some rotation time on your DPS, it's generally recommended to ignore it entirely unless you pick it up by sheer luck.

sections.heading: Meta Position & Conclusion
paragraphs: While Baizhi can have a very short rotation with good buffs to Hypercarry teams on paper, she has a lot of issues that make this not work in practice. First of all, her Forte stack generation is completely dependent on her Basic Attacks hitting enemies for damage. Not only do they only hit grounded targets, aggressive enemies will force you into using Perfect Dodges that will slow Baizhi's rotation down significantly because her Forte generates so much of the Concerto she needs. This makes her inconsistent against both aggressive and airborne enemies, and that's basically all boss enemies aside from Matrix Mimic specifically.

Not only that, but her buffing is all single-target instead of party-wide. While nothing expires on swap, she is still incompatible with Quickswap playstyles and off-field damage dealers, because the healing on her Outro has to regularly activate in order to buff the character it affects, her Euphonia buff is inherently single-target, and her swap-in attack is really bad and slows down her rotations more than it helps.

Finally, Verina and Buling are both free generalist options for healing and party-wide buffing that work exactly like Baizhi, only better (and that's excluding limited Supports that are on another level). Their kits are coherent and have attacks that string together nicely, while providing better buffing than Baizhi. In the case of Buling, while her best rotation is slightly longer than Baizhi's, in practice it is much more consistent and it doesn't matter too much for team rotation time. Against most enemies in the game, unless they're standing next to completely still, Buling is always better. Verina is always faster and has more buffs that apply party-wide, while Buling is more Quickswap-compatible and has extra synergies with Electro Flare and Skill Damage that Baizhi does not cover. Buling also retains party-wide buffing capabilities with the same total buffing profile as Baizhi, if we exclude random Euphonia pick-up chances (which you realistically should exclude).

However, Baizhi has one big pro going for her: without a proper build beyond simply satisfying Energy Regen requirements, without any investments on her character skills and even her character level, and optionally without a Concerto weapon, Baizhi already pretty much provides the full extent of what she's capable of. She requires practically nothing to get up and running, so if you really need to use her, you just can. And that counts for something, because despite her use cases being extremely restricted and her many flaws, at least she's not an investment commitment. She can serve as a worse Verina/Buling alternative for low priority Matrix teams, or for beginner accounts, if you really need it.

In conclusion, Baizhi is generally not worth investing into, and that's okay. She only needs her Energy Regen requirements met to properly operate as a general healing/buffing Support that is frankly not useful for endgame content, but can at least serve as a worse alternative to Verina, Buling, or any limited Support in the same niche, while requiring barely any investment to operate. While this makes her useless for most accounts, her practically costless investment requirements can make her useful for specific use cases.
